messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
When you throw a ball straight up, its only vertical acceleration comes from Earth’s gravity—there's no other force acting on it (ignoring drag).  
So the acceleration is simply:

\[
a \;=\; -\,g \;\approx\; -9.8~\text{m s}^{-2}
\]

(The minus sign indicates that the acceleration points downwards, opposite to the direction of motion.)  

This value holds whether the ball starts at \(0\), \(5\) m/s, or any other speed—the acceleration doesn’t change during free‑fall.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" They likely want gravitational acceleration downward (i.e., -9.8 m/s^2). But maybe they think about max height calculation? Actually question ambiguous: "acceleration a ball will reach" might mean what acceleration does it experience while moving upward? That would be constant negative g ~ -9.81 m/s². So answer: approximately -9.8 m/s².
